extracted.intended_audience: public relations students, educators, and practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for writing, timing, submitting, and evaluating press (news) releases as part of public relations programs. Emphasizes management considerations, objectives, media relations, distribution channels (wire, hand delivery), and evaluation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Define explicit objectives for public relations writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC heading: WRITING OBJECTIVES) Implies that writing should be planned to meet program/communication objectives and aligned with organizational goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum Objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive for maximum objectivity in public relations writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC heading: MAXIMUM OBJECTIVITY) Guidance implies maintaining factual, unbiased tone where appropriate; supports credibility of releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully review and verify sources used in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC heading: SOURCE REVIEW) Implies checking accuracy, permissions, and reliability of sources before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long‑Range Implications / Consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess long‑range implications and ensure consistency of messages with organizational strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC heading: LONG‑RANGE IMPLICATIONS/CONSISTENCY) Consider how a release fits with long‑term positioning and prior communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Achieving Maximum Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft messages and formats to achieve maximum impact for the intended publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC heading: ACHIEVING MAXIMUM IMPACT) Implies selection of lead, angle, facts, and placement to maximize news value and audience uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Matter of Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow appropriate stylistic conventions for PR writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC heading: A MATTER OF STYLE) Covers tone, clarity, readability, and media preferences for style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating Your Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically evaluate the quality and effectiveness of written materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC heading: EVALUATING YOUR WRITING) Implies use of checklists/readership feedback to judge clarity, accuracy, and fit with objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press Releases — Management Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider press releases within the larger PR management framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: MANAGEMENT CONSIDERATIONS) Explicit subpoints listed for press releases: Model of Public Relations; Objectives; Which Programs?; Communication Behavior of Publics; Cost in Time and Money; Evaluation. The release should be planned according to these considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model of Public Relations (as applied to releases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose and apply the appropriate PR model when using press releases (e.g., public information, two‑way models).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC subpoint under Management Considerations) The choice of model affects objectives, tone, and whether releases are informational, persuasive, or dialogic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (for press releases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set clear objectives for each press release (what effect it should produce).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC subpoint) Objectives must link to program goals and be measurable as part of evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which Programs? (appropriateness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide which programs or campaigns should use press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC subpoint) Determine when a news release is the right tactic versus other techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication Behavior of Publics (audience analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for the communication behavior of target publics when preparing releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC subpoint) Tailor timing, content, and channel to how different publics seek and receive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost in Time and Money (resource consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Weigh the time and monetary costs of preparing and distributing releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC subpoint) Include staff time, production, distribution fees (wire services), and follow‑up costs in planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation (of press‑release outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan how the effects of a release will be measured and evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC subpoint) Link evaluation to objectives (e.g., coverage, agenda setting, message retention, behavioral outcomes). Use the evaluation methods described in the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: The News Release (core elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce a properly constructed news release containing the elements journalists expect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC heading: THE NEWS RELEASE) The book contains a 'News‑Release Checklist' (see separate entry) that operationalizes required elements for editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: News‑Release Checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: A checklist of required elements to include in a news release for editorial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC heading: News‑Release Checklist) Although full checklist text is not in this chunk, the checklist is presented as a standard evaluative/production tool for news releases (headline, dateline, lead, nut graph, contact information, boilerplate, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadcast Releases — Spokesperson Availability
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing broadcast releases, ensure a spokesperson is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC heading: BROADCAST RELEASES: Make a Spokesperson Available) For radio/TV releases, provide on‑air talent or interviewees and prepare them for media contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing the Release — Embargoes and Delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Time releases strategically, using embargoes or hand delivery when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: TIMING THE RELEASE) Specific tactics: Using an 'Embargo'; Hand Delivery May Be Necessary. Consider media deadlines and competitive timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting the Press Release — Selectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Be selective about when and to whom you submit releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC heading: SUBMITTING THE PRESS RELEASE) 'When to Be Selective'—target distribution to relevant outlets to avoid wasting resources and irritating journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using the PR Wire — Mechanics and Retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand and use newswire services effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: USING THE PR WIRE) Subpoints: How the Service Works; The Information‑Retrieval Link. Know wire costs, formatting, and how editors/search systems retrieve releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Relations — What Helps and Hurts
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow practices that help (and avoid those that hurt) relationships with the news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: MEDIA RELATIONS) Includes guidance on courtesy, accuracy, timeliness, avoiding conflicts, and respecting journalistic norms to improve pickup of releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding Journalists' Behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Use theory and empirical findings about journalists' behavior to tailor release content and approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC subpoints: Theoretical Explanations of Journalists’ Behavior; Levels of Analysis; Two Studies of Journalist Publics) Apply knowledge of news values and constraints in crafting releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Agenda Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how effectively releases influence the media agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: MEDIA RELATIONS OBJECTIVES AND EVALUATION) Use agenda‑setting research and methods to assess whether the release shaped media coverage topics and prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting Public Relations Objectives (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define PR objectives in terms of organizational effects and publics' responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC/Part II headings: DEFINING AND CHOOSING GOALS AND OBJECTIVES; THINK IN TERMS OF EFFECT; TWO‑WAY SYMMETRIC GOAL‑SETTING; SETTING PUBLIC RELATIONS OBJECTIVES; Making MBO Work) Objectives should be outcome‑oriented, specify who decides, and be compatible with two‑way symmetric principles when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Research — Stages and Integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate evaluation as an essential stage of PR management and use evaluation results to inform decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: EVALUATION RESEARCH; STAGES OF EVALUATION; EVALUATION AND THE MANAGEMENT PROCESS; APPLYING EVALUATION RESULTS TO DECISIONS; PROCESS EVALUATIONS; WHO SHOULD EVALUATE?) Evaluation is ongoing, tied to management, and can be formative, process, or summative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Methods — Surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Use surveys as an evaluation method for communication effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: EVALUATION METHODS — Surveys) Suitable for measuring awareness, retention, attitudes, and self‑reported behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Methods — Experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use experiments to test causal effects of messages or tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: EVALUATION METHODS — Experiments) Useful for establishing causal relationships between releases and changes in knowledge/attitudes/behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Methods — Secondary Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Use secondary data sources as part of evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: Secondary Data) Include existing audience metrics, circulation, broadcast logs, and organizational data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Methods — Qualitative Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Use qualitative methods to understand 'what's happening' and contextual effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: Qualitative Analysis; A Sense of 'What's Happening') Methods include interviews, focus groups, and content analysis to interpret responses to releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Methods — Time Budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use time budgets and network analysis to define and evaluate scheduling and resource use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: Time Budgets; Network Analysis referenced elsewhere) Helpful for planning implementation timing (e.g., critical path, Gantt, PERT) and measuring process efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures Used in Social‑Science Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Select appropriate question types and measures for evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: MEASURES USED IN SOCIAL SCIENCE RESEARCH) Examples: Fact Questions; Evaluative Questions; Information Questions; Self‑Perception Questions — choose depending on objective (knowledge, attitude, behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample Measures of PR Objectives — Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure whether communication objectives (exposure, comprehension) were met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: SAMPLE MEASURES — Communication) Includes metrics of message delivery, readership/viewership, and understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample Measures of PR Objectives — Retention of Messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how well target publics retained messages from releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: Retention of Messages) Use follow‑up surveys or recall tests to assess retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample Measures of PR Objectives — Acceptance of Cognitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure acceptance of factual claims or cognitive elements presented in releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: Acceptance of Cognitions) Assess whether audiences accept the information intellectually, separate from attitudinal change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample Measures — Coorientational Measure of Understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure mutual understanding between organization and publics (coorientation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: A Coorientational Measure of Understanding) Use coorientation approaches to compare organizational and public perceptions and beliefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample Measures — Attitude (Evaluation / Behavioral Intent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure attitudinal change or behavioral intentions resulting from releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: Attitude (Evaluation/Behavioral Intent)) Use validated attitude scales and intention measures tied to objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample Measures — Overt Behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure actual behavioral outcomes influenced by PR efforts (e.g., event attendance, donations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: Overt Behavior) Where possible, measure observable actions rather than just self‑reported intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample Measures — Combination of Methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine multiple methods to evaluate release effects comprehensively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: Combination of Methods) Triangulate surveys, content analysis, and behavioral data to strengthen inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Constraints — Right to Communicate
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand legal rights and access issues when communicating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: LEGAL CONSTRAINTS; THE RIGHT TO COMMUNICATE) Includes corporate partisan expression and access to broadcast media and information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Constraints — Libel and Slander
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid defamation risks in releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: RESTRICTIONS ON THE RIGHT TO COMMUNICATE — LIBEL AND SLANDER) Take care with factual assertions about individuals and avoid statements that could lead to punitive damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Constraints — Copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect copyright when using third‑party material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: COPYRIGHT) Always obtain permission for copyrighted material used in releases and handouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Constraints — Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe privacy rules in deciding what is 'news' vs. 'promotion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: PRIVACY) Determine whether content intrudes on individuals' privacy and whether consent is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Constraints — Financial Reporting Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with rules on disclosure when releases involve financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: FINANCIAL REPORTING REQUIREMENTS) Be aware of prospectus, annual report, and timely disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Constraints — Regulation of Advertising and Consumer Protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure releases and related communications comply with advertising and consumer‑protection regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: REGULATION OF ADVERTISING; CONSUMER PROTECTION) Beware of claims that could be treated as deceptive advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Constraints — Rights of Employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect employees' rights when internal communications or releases affect them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: RIGHTS OF EMPLOYEES) Consider labor law and internal‑communication implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Constraints — Lobbyists and Foreign Agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow registration and disclosure rules when representing governments or lobbying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: LOBBYISTS AND FOREIGN AGENTS; Representing Foreign Governments) Be mindful of legal requirements for advocacy and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living with the Law (practical guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt practical procedures to live within legal constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (TOC: LIVING WITH THE LAW) Establish review processes, legal clearance, and training to reduce legal risk when issuing releases.
